benchmark_cold_warm_combined_single_proc.description: benchmark_cold_warm.py run end-to-end (cold start, then born-digital warm runs, then scanned warm runs, all in one process)
benchmark_cold_warm_combined_single_proc.note: Both crashes occurred at the same point: immediately after the arabic_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec recognition model was loaded, before the first conversions result was printed. Reordering fixture creation relative to adapter construction did not prevent the second crash. Isolated single-path runs (born_digital only, scanned only) in separate fresh processes both succeeded 3/3 warm runs with no crash -- consistent with the broader UNRESOLVED finding that the fault correlates with doing multiple/varied conversions in one long-lived process, not with any single isolated factor identified so far.

stable_workloads_this_session: single conversion of any kind, alone in a process
5x repeated sequential runs of the same scanned document
12x sequential scanned-only conversions across 4 fixtures (prior isolation runs)
unstable_workloads_this_session: benchmark_cold_warm.py full single-process run (cold start + born-digital warm runs + scanned warm runs) -- crashed 2/2 attempts (exit -1073741819)
investigation_summary.access_violation_trigger_condition: No single factor fully explains all sequential-workload observations. Initially appeared tied to mixing a vector-text (reportlab) PDF with a scanned/raster PDF in one process (reproduced in several bare script attempts); that hypothesis was DISPROVEN by a later run in which the crash occurred after ~34 purely scanned-fixture conversions with no vector-text PDF involved. Best-supported working theory for SEQUENTIAL workloads: probability correlates with CUMULATIVE native engine call volume in one long-lived process, not input shape. Root cause (PaddleOCR / PaddleX / PaddlePaddle native runtime / pytest interaction) could not be isolated further within this investigation's scope.
investigation_summary.concurrency_finding: Calling PaddleOcrAdapter().convert() from 2 threads at once (ThreadPoolExecutor, max_workers=2) reproducibly fails on EVERY attempt made in this investigation, via one of THREE failure modes: (1) a clean Python-level 'IndexError: invalid vector<bool> subscript' raised from paddlex/inference/pipelines/_parallel.py when 2 threads share ONE adapter instance, captured verbatim in bounded_concurrent_scanned_documents above; (2) a native Windows access violation (exit -1073741819 / 0xC0000005), reproduced even when each thread used its OWN separate PaddleOcrAdapter() instance, ruling out Python-level instance-sharing as the sole cause; or (3) a native Windows heap corruption (exit code whose unsigned/hex form is 0xC0000374 / STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION), also captured verbatim in bounded_concurrent_scanned_documents above. Practical recommendation: do not call this adapter concurrently from multiple threads in one process on Windows with this pinned version; serialize all conversions.
investigation_summary.known_related_finding: paddlepaddle==3.0.0 (an UNPINNED, rejected version) reproducibly crashed with a native Windows access violation (exit code -1073741819 / 0xC0000005) during capability discovery for this same adapter's OCR call, on this same machine, for a SINGLE conversion -- see adapter.py module docstring 'Version pinning'. That is a separate, fully deterministic finding for a rejected version; it is distinct from the intermittent finding above, which occurs even with the pinned version.

grouped_pytest_run_ocr_routing_combined.description: pytest tests/test_ocr_applied_always.py tests/test_vector_pdf_capability.py run together in one subprocess (via run_tests.ps1 grouping)
grouped_pytest_run_ocr_routing_combined.note: Crashed partway through test_vector_pdf_capability.py::test_single_born_digital_conversion_succeeds_and_is_classified_correctly, immediately after 3/3 tests in test_ocr_applied_always.py passed. Re-running test_vector_pdf_capability.py alone (no combination) succeeded 2/2. This is another real occurrence of the general sequential-workload UNRESOLVED finding, not a new distinct bug -- consistent with the cumulative-call-volume theory. run_tests.ps1 was updated to run these two files as separate subprocess groups to avoid this combination.
